clue.text: Lay by beach drinking Tango

indicators.note: something drinking takes a thing into itself, so the beach word swallows the letter

parts.note: a beach is the seaside
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker at the beach sipping a fizzy Tango.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British fizzy drink, which makes 'drinking Tango' read as a beach snack rather than an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something by is to reserve it for later, the same sense as putting it aside.

clue.text: Soldiers carrying much less mass for instance

indicators.note: the soldiers hold the trimmed word between them, as if carrying it

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment

indicators.note: less means without, so the letter for mass is taken out of much

parts.note: m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Troops, for example, lugging a much lighter load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like weight in the surface, matching 'much less'; here it is just the physics symbol for mass, taken out of the word much.
explanation.definitionFit: Such as introduces an example, just like for instance does; the two phrases are interchangeable.

clue.text: Overhaul locomotives leaving one half of platform

indicators.note: one leaving means the letter for one departs from the locomotives word

parts.note: locomotives pull trains
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half of the word platform is kept, here its back half

explanation.surface: Engines pulling out from part of a station platform for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of TRAINS for TRANS; 'half of' gives FORM, the back half of PLATFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul something is to change it thoroughly, which is what transforming it does.

clue.text: Problem with speech? Change the middle for political leader

indicators.note: the central letter of the speech word is swapped for another letter, giving a new name

parts.note: a stammer is a speech impediment

explanation.surface: A politician's halting delivery could be fixed by reworking the middle of the speech.
explanation.walkthrough: STAMMER has seven letters; its fourth, an M, becomes R. Keir Starmer is a leader of the UK Labour Party and Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer leads the British Labour Party, so he is a political leader.

clue.text: Old- fashioned parent ringing teen on a regular basis

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the parent word encircles the letters

parts.note: a dad is a parent

indicators.note: taking every other letter of teen, the first and third

explanation.surface: An out-of-touch father regularly phoning his teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated belongs to an earlier time and so seems out of style.

clue.text: Wine inside ship's jars

indicators.note: the wine goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for a ship
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Wine stored in jars aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like a noun for containers; it is the verb meaning jolts.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to jolt or startle someone, as shocks do.

clue.text: Relative triumph finally with American pop group

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of triumph

parts.note: its last letter is H
a pop group is a band

explanation.surface: A family member's big win at last, alongside an American pop act.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a relation by marriage, so a relative in the family sense.

clue.text: Pal cold at home wearing hat with temperature dropping

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: the trimmed hat sits around the home word, as if worn over it
the letter for temperature drops out of hat

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
in means at home

explanation.surface: A friend indoors in the cold, wearing a hat as the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: China is cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In cockney rhyming slang china plate rhymes with mate, so china means a friend.

clue.text: Tension — feeling keeping us quiet

indicators.note: the feeling word keeps the other letters held inside it

parts.note: a sense is a feeling
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A tense mood, with everyone told to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty of waiting, a state of tension.

clue.text: Turn game off, creating dispute

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Switching off the game console sparks a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn game off' reads as switching off a game; 'off' is the anagram signal for TURN GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a quarrel or disagreement, the same as a dispute.

clue.text: Reacts as critic gets upset about hotel features

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled letters go round the hotel letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A reviewer bristles at what a hotel offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' looks like a verb about the hotel; it is the noun meaning traits.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics are the distinguishing traits of something, its features.

clue.text: Accepted a second problem with eastern diamonds

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a further puzzle involving gems from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means taken for granted or taken on, as with something accepted.

clue.text: A Parisian admitting a fight in the dark

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the French word contains the others

parts.note: une is French for a, as said in Paris
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman confessing to a scuffle at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dark' suggests a night fight; it is the definition, meaning uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark about something is to be ignorant of it, not knowing.

clue.text: Bird food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in British slang both bird and ... mean time served in prison
second meaning: oatmeal cooked in milk or water, a breakfast dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like the creature, so 'Bird food' reads as seed; in British slang doing bird or doing porridge is serving a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is British slang for a prison term, and also the oat breakfast cereal.

clue.text: Perhaps T. Rex finale of Bolan in US radio broadcast

indicators.note: the letter goes in the scrambled radio letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered
the finale is the last letter of Bolan

explanation.surface: The close of a Marc Bolan song played on American radio.
explanation.walkthrough: T. Rex was Marc Bolan's glam-rock band, but here it is Tyrannosaurus rex, the prehistoric reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannosaurus rex is an example of an extinct prehistoric reptile; 'Perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Medic's bandaging king's cuts

indicators.note: bandaging wraps around, so the medic letters enclose the king

parts.note: a doc is a medic, with the s from the possessive
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A doctor dressing the monarch's wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' reads as wounds; it is the verb, as in docking pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages or a tail is to cut them short, so docks means reduces.

clue.text: Bird eating nuts cut head in pit?

indicators.note: the bird takes the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: a condor is a large vulture

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bird pecking nuts as its head is cut, down a mine pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit is the orchestra pit, not a mine; its head is the one leading the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra sits in the pit at a theatre, and the person directing it leads from there.

clue.text: Went on board ship following European doctor and Edward

indicators.note: following means the ship comes after the European and doctor letters

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
Noah's ark is the most famous ship of all
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A European medic and a man called Edward board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or aircraft at the start of a journey.

clue.text: Maiden in the morning initially bitten by a snake

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a.m. means in the morning

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of bitten

parts.note: its first letter is B

explanation.surface: A young woman bitten by a snake early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is a cricket over in which no runs are scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a highly venomous African snake.

clue.text: Fed up? Done any blunders?

indicators.note: blunders means goes wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is cross because they have made mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed up means irritated or exasperated, the same as being annoyed.

clue.text: Perceiving no sign of nerves in golf

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer showing no hint of nerves on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing something means becoming aware of it by sight or sense, the same as perceiving it.

clue.text: Tooth decay hampers last of polar bears

indicators.note: hampers here means holds back, so the decay word encloses the letter

parts.note: caries is the medical word for tooth decay

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of polar

explanation.surface: Rotting teeth trouble the last of the polar bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals after 'polar'; it is the verb, meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry or support it, so bears and carries match.

clue.text: Writer with note editor enclosed

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author whose memo has been tucked in by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' suggests a letter enclosure; it means penned in, like sheep in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that are penned are shut in a pen, kept confined or enclosed.

clue.text: A small cuckoo nest, son agrees

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A little cuckoo in its nest, and a son who goes along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoo famously lays eggs in other birds' nests, so 'cuckoo nest' reads as a bird; 'cuckoo' signals the anagram of NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to express approval or agreement, so assents means agrees.

clue.text: Band rocked on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard aloud, so the answer sounds like the word for rocked

parts.note: rocked means moved from side to side, swayed

explanation.surface: A rock group playing on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Suede are a British indie rock band from the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is the name of a British rock group, so it is a band.

clue.text: Scent for each upper class female brought back by this writer

parts.note: per means for each

indicators.note: brought back means the two letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: U is the old British shorthand for upper-class usage
this writer refers to the setter, giving me

explanation.surface: A smell for each posh lady, brought home by the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume is a fragrant liquid worn for its pleasant smell, a scent.

clue.text: Section of alp is terrific ski run

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a mountain is wonderful for skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a marked trail of compacted snow for skiing down.

clue.text: Stay calm — don't go topless!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom urging someone not to lose their temper

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for not getting angry is read literally as advice to keep clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells an agitated person to calm down; literally it forbids removing one's top.

clue.text: Daughter shows fears

parts.note: D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter
a dial reads a value when it shows it

explanation.surface: A girl reveals what scares her.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to fear it greatly in anticipation.

clue.text: Certainly getting in drink is considered

indicators.note: the word for certainly gets in, inside the drink

parts.note: mead is a drink made from fermented honey
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Taking a drink is surely a thoughtful choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is careful and deliberate, one that has been considered.
